# Energy execution review: Wednesday 11 November 2026
**Fixed session: 00:00-24:00 UTC. Booking knowledge frozen at 12 November 09:20:15 UTC.** This notebook stays on this date when reopened. Refresh is off.

**Desk aggregate:** 3,007 active trades (2,757 exchange, 149 broker, 101 OTC), USD 4.386bn gross notional. Five-minute signed markout **+$460,908**, including +$218,642 exchange, +$162,470 broker and +$79,797 OTC. This is a horizon valuation measure before fees and hedging, not realised desk P&L. Aggregate gains conceal the following:

| Finding | Evidence | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| WTI broker flow shows adverse selection | 24 trades, 919,000 bbl; -1.01 bps at fill, -6.16 bps / -$49,275 at 5m, -10.30 bps / -$92,855 at 15m. Naive 5m t=-4.56. | Highest-confidence execution concern. 13 matched trades underperform same-contract, same-side exchange fills in the same 4h bucket by 9.34 bps at 5m (t=-3.91). Fresh-quote subset: 21 trades, -6.29 bps. |
| Counterparty watchlist | UTILITY_02: n=6, -13.60 bps, -$134,140 at 5m, t=-4.64. UTILITY_10: n=6, -13.34 bps, -$15,093, t=-3.75. | Small samples and many comparisons. Only 2 / 4 respectively have matched controls. Investigate, do not infer misconduct or certainty. |
| Gas and power market surge | Jan-27 TTF and NBP rise about 7%, UK power about 6%, around 09:30-09:50 UTC; sub-second maximum quote gaps for these contracts. | Common market move explains extreme sell markouts. Venue clearing accounts do not identify the opposing trader. |
| Production model mispricing | 10:00-24:00 winter-month contemporaneous quote bias: champion_v1 TTF -389.44, NBP -388.47, UKPWR -323.80 bps; challenger_v2 about zero. 6,720 marks per curve/version. | Pricing/model issue. Data do not establish that this model caused any fill. |
| Gasoil apparent execution loss | ICE n=442, all aggressive; initial -1.52 bps vs 1.49 bps half-spread, -$65,925. 5m -1.34 bps / -$47,363. | Primarily spread crossing. No progressive post-fill deterioration at desk aggregate. |
| TTF valuation anomaly | trader_11 manual Q1-27 marks, 08:00-08:29: n=30, mean +EUR 2.4986/MWh above contemporaneous mid. | Mark governance/valuation, not evidence of poor fills. |
| Booking incompleteness | 8 broker and 26 OTC Wednesday trades booked on Thursday; 15 amendment/cancellation events. | Trade-time review must use latest active versions. A Wednesday booking-date extract misses activity. |

**Reading the panels:** negative markout is adverse to the desk. Offsets include -30s, fill, 1s, 10s, 1m, 5m and 15m. Tables include naive t-statistics and weighted bps. Counterparty detail is controlled by the notebook variable `counterparty`.

## Method and evidence limits

- Session is the entire UTC calendar day. The question did not specify a venue-local session. Quotes extend through 12 November 09:20, so all Wednesday +15m observations have forward coverage.
- Universe uses the latest trade event known by **12 November 09:20:15 UTC**, then removes cancellations and selects Wednesday **trade time**. Exchange quote sampling preserves `energy_fills.ts` nanoseconds; booking corrections supply the final quantity and price. Broker and OTC timestamps have microsecond precision. Exchange and ledger rows are joined by trade_id, never counted twice.
- Signed markout = sign(qty) x (prevailing future mid - fill price). At offset 0 this is the negative cost against mid. Quote selection is backward as of each target time, never a look-ahead. Stale observations remain visible in raw panels; panels 14-15 show coverage and a 30-second sensitivity filter.
- USD markout = signed price difference x abs(qty) x instrument px_factor x fixed session-end FX. EURUSD **1.10761**, GBPUSD **1.32753**. NBP is pence/therm, so multiply by **0.01**. Quantities are already native physical units; do not multiply by contract lot size or delivery hours again. No adding raw pence, euros and dollars.
- Mean bps weights trades equally. Weighted bps divides aggregate USD markout by aggregate USD gross notional. Large profitable power trades explain why voice channels can have positive dollars and negative equally weighted mean bps.
- Matched controls use contract, buy/sell side and a four-hour UTC bucket. They are a sensitivity check, not randomised causal attribution. Coverage is incomplete, execution style and sizes differ, and peer sets can be reused. `peer_comparisons` is not an independent trade count.
- `naive_t` = trade mean / (sample standard deviation / sqrt(n)). Serial dependence, shared market shocks and scanning many segments overstate confidence. Do not interpret the panels as multiple-testing-adjusted significance or evidence of intent. Single trades and n=2-3 cells are hypotheses.
- OTC/broker passive status is **unknown**, never inferred from the false placeholder used to align UNION column types. Passive splits apply only to exchange fills.
- Exchange counterparty values ICE_CLEAR_EU, ECC and CME_CLEARING identify clearing, not the economic aggressor. Broker and OTC counterparty codes are identifiable, but beneficial ownership and quote/reject messages are absent.
- Fees, hedging, order arrival/decision prices, rejected quotes, queue position and model routing are not available. Markouts do not prove last-look abuse, information leakage or total desk profitability. Tuesday is the only complete prior-day baseline: WTI broker 5m -0.85 bps (n=26) versus Wednesday -6.16 (n=24); this is a one-session deterioration.
- The model chart uses the existing graded view's preceding completed 1m bar; the independent raw ASOF check avoids treating that lag as model bias. Winter means delivery month Nov-Feb, consistent with the existing view. Manual-mark diagnostics are kept separate from fill benchmarks.
- Static findings above preserve the reviewed numbers. SQL remains fixed to the historical date and booking cutoff. Reruns require underlying data to remain retained. Export this notebook from the tab menu for an additional copy.

## Coverage audit

| Data objects | Check and result |
|---|---|
| energy_fills; energy_trade_events; energy_book_asof; energy_book_restated; energy_trade_events_latest | Inspected schemas and asof/restated definitions; 2,757 Wednesday exchange fills; 3,007 latest active trades. Two cancelled broker tickets excluded; 15 lifecycle updates and 34 next-day original bookings identified. |
| energy_quotes; energy_quotes_10s; energy_quotes_1m; energy_quotes_5m; energy_quotes_1d; energy_mid_1m_day | Raw feeds have no crossed or null bids on Wednesday; horizon matches available. Stale quotes occur in quieter tenors. Three front winter contracts have maximum gaps below one second during the surge. Rollup schemas and lineage inspected; 1m/5m used only for context, raw quotes for TCA. |
| energy_instruments; energy_listings; energy_instrument_master; energy_tenors; energy_tenors_asof | Unit/FX multipliers inspected; 243 unique instruments, up to two listings per contract. Use instrument table to avoid listing fanout. March/October delivery-hour differences are consistent with daylight-saving hours; no unit rescaling inferred from them. |
| energy_curve_marks; energy_curve_marks_1h; energy_curve_marks_latest; energy_marks_asof; energy_marks_live; energy_strip_gaps_day | Source/version inspection and raw mark/quote comparison reveal 30 manual TTF Q1 marks. Derived view definitions/lineage reviewed; current-day strip-gap output is unsuitable as Wednesday evidence and not used. Other valuation reconciliation is outside this TCA. |
| energy_model_prices; energy_model_graded_day | Both versions have fresh input timestamps. Full Wednesday winter/summer comparison plus Tuesday baseline; production winter underpricing independently checked against contemporaneous raw quotes. Summer mean bias is near zero in the graded view. |
| energy_fx_asof; energy_usd_factor_asof | Factor definition inspected. Avoid moving now()-based FX in a historical review; use explicit Wednesday close FX from raw quotes instead. |
| energy_position_snapshots; energy_ledger; energy_positions_live; energy_positions_live_by_venue; energy_positions_running_day; energy_limits | Schemas and lineage inspected. Snapshot aggregate net quantities over available dates are below listed limits (largest ratio 35.54%). Limits are dated 12 November, so this is a sanity check, not proof of historical intraday compliance. No complete position reconciliation or realised-P&L claim made. |
| energy_settlements | 486 exchange settlement rows over 10-11 November; no null prices. Settlement times differ by curve (16:30 versus 19:30), so not substituted for common-horizon execution benchmarks. |
| energy_iv_marks | 124,024 VOL_SVC marks, IV 0.23167-0.72852 and positive time to expiry. No option fills identified; not an execution benchmark. |
| energy_da_prices | 72 N2EX hourly rows over 10-12 November; publication timestamps inspected. Separate day-ahead auction product, not a benchmark for forward futures fills. |
| energy_lineage | All listed derived dependencies valid; both position live views active. Lineage health does not certify economic reconciliation. |

**Next operational checks:** review WTI broker pricing/hedging and quote timestamps; inspect UTILITY_02/10 trade details with a longer history; investigate production winter-model response after the market surge and the manual TTF mark override. No trading or production configuration was changed.
